newsitem.title: FRANCE: Two would-be bombers arrested in Corsica - police.
newsitem.headline: Two would-be bombers arrested in Corsica - police.

text.p: Two professional explosives experts have been arrested placing a bomb outside the home of a leading Corsican politician and industrialist, French police said on Saturday.

The French Mediterranean island of Corsica has been the scene of hundreds of bombings by suspected separatist guerrillas in the past few years but few arrests have been made, largely because of the island's traditional "omerta" law of silence.
The suspects, employees of a private firm involved in public works projects, were arrested on Friday in northern Corsica, police said.
Neither they nor their target was identified but police said a search of the suspects' homes led to the discovery of several other explosive charges primed to be set off.
The last successful bombing was on Friday as the troubled Mediterranean island and mainland France awaited the formal end of a guerrilla "truce" already shattered by dozens of blasts.

The 10-month-old truce declared by the hardline Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC)-Historic Wing is due to expire on Saturday. But it effectively lapsed when attacks resumed after secret talks with Paris collapsed during the summer.
Some 2,000 police and paramilitary gendarmes are based on the island to cope with any upsurge in nationalist activity.
